item.title: Our position on open-weights models
item.description:
📝 Reports suggest that some US officials are considering banning the use of Chinese open-weights models by US companies. Distillation is a much more compute-efficient process than training models from scratch. We should have policy interventions to deter this behavior.
🔗 Read more: https://www.anthropic.com/news/position-open-weights-models

item.title: Benchmarking Opus 5 on SlopCodeBench
item.description:
📝 benching opus 5 on slopcodebench On Friday I ran three claude models (Opus 4. The big headline is that Opus 5 got a 24% on the small subset of the benchmark that I ran - not much higher than Opus 4. Model writes code for ck1 Eval harness runs black-box tests against ck1 Model writes code for ck2 Eval runs black-box tests for ck1 and ck2 etc Again, the strict pass criteria means that if a model bungles something in checkpoint 4, it can't pass the following checkpoints because that failing part of the code carries forward (unless the model indavertently fixes an eval case in checkpoint 6 that was broken in checkpoint 4, but we didn't see this happen in practice).
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/humanlayer/advanced-context-engineering-for-coding-agents/blob/main/benchmarking-opus-5-on-slop-code-bench.md

item.title: Astronauts describe persistent 'observer' sensation after 6 month missions
item.description:
📝 But flight surgeons and crew psychologists who debrief astronauts after six-month rotations describe it often enough that it has become a recognizable readjustment pattern — an observer sensation that lingers for weeks, sometimes months, after splashdown. Returning astronauts describe walking into their own homes and feeling like they are visiting them. That extra processing load can feel like watching yourself perform basic tasks.
🔗 Read more: https://spacedaily.com/sd-v-astronauts-returning-from-six-month-missions-describe-a-persistent-observer-sensation-the-feeling-of-watching-their-own-lives-from-a-half-step-outside-the-frame-weeks-after-theyr/

item.title: DConf 2026 in London
item.description:
